title: SQLite Contention Management
purpose: Prevent SQLite WAL write contention from becoming the coordination bottleneck. Empirical benchmarks show a hard efficiency cliff at 4 concurrent writers (throughput drops to 36% of single-thread) and p99 latency explodes from 0ms at 1 thread to 230ms at 32 threads. This SOP defines maximum writer limits, partitioning strategies, backoff procedures, and monitoring thresholds to keep operations within safe contention bounds.
scope: All multi-agent operations using SQLite WAL for coordination state (hub databases, work queues, scratchpads, channel stores). Applies to coordinator_hub.py, help_protocol.py, work_stealing.py, and direct_channels.py.

key_findings.key_observation: p50 latency stays constant at ~0.24ms across all thread counts. The problem is SQLite WAL write serialization causing extreme TAIL latency (p99). Median operations are fast; it is the contention-caused retries that destroy throughput.
key_findings.cliff_at_4_threads: At 4 concurrent writers, throughput drops to 36% and p99 hits 34ms. This is the practical maximum for a single database.
key_findings.cliff_at_8_threads: At 8 concurrent writers, only 16% throughput remains. Each additional writer beyond 4 yields diminishing returns.
key_findings.thundering_herd: 10 threads competing for 50 work items: p95 jumps to 79ms vs 0.66ms single-thread (120x amplification). Work stealing is double-steal safe but latency-expensive.
key_findings.cross_reference: Combined with SOP-032 optimal team size of 5-8 agents, teams of 5-8 MUST use partitioned write access or a coordinator proxy to avoid the 4-thread cliff.

procedures.title: Determine Writer Count Per Database
procedures.action: Before operation start, count the maximum number of agents that will write concurrently to each SQLite database. Include the coordinator as a writer.

rules.safe_zone: 1-3 concurrent writers. Throughput remains above 36%. p99 stays under 35ms.
rules.caution_zone: 4 concurrent writers. Throughput at 36%. p99 at 34ms. This is the absolute maximum for a single database without partitioning.
rules.danger_zone: 5-8 concurrent writers. Throughput at 16%. p99 at 55ms. Requires immediate partitioning.
rules.critical_zone: 9+ concurrent writers. Throughput below 6%. p99 above 130ms. Operations will experience severe degradation.

procedures.output: Writer count per database documented in operation plan

procedures.title: Partition Databases for Teams of 5+
procedures.action: For any team with 5+ agents writing to a shared database, partition into multiple databases with no more than 4 writers each.

sub_coordinator_pattern.description: Split team into sub-groups of 3-4 agents, each with its own coordinator and database. A top-level coordinator reads from all sub-databases.
sub_coordinator_pattern.example: 8-agent team -> 2 sub-coordinators of 4 agents each, each with own hub DB. Top coordinator reads both.

single_writer_proxy.description: All agents send write requests to a single coordinator agent who serializes writes to one database. Agents only read (which is contention-free in WAL mode).
single_writer_proxy.example: 7-agent team -> 1 coordinator writes all status updates. 6 agents read status but never write directly.

functional_partitioning.description: Separate databases by function: one for hub/status, one for work queues, one for channels. Each database has fewer writers.
functional_partitioning.example: research-hub.db (coordinator writes), build-queue.db (3 build agents write), test-channels.db (4 test agents write)
functional_partitioning.best_for: Mixed operations with distinct functional areas

procedures.output: Database partitioning plan with writer assignments

procedures.title: Configure Retry and Backoff Parameters
procedures.action: Set appropriate retry budgets based on expected contention level.

1_to_4_writers.rationale: Standard configuration handles contention at this level

5_to_8_writers.rationale: Higher retry count accommodates increased tail latency. Jitter prevents synchronized retries.

9_to_16_writers.backoff_strategy: Exponential backoff with jitter, base delay 50ms
9_to_16_writers.rationale: p99 exceeds 130ms at 16 threads. Need more retries and longer delays to avoid cascading failures.

17_plus_writers.backoff_strategy: Exponential backoff with jitter, base delay 100ms
17_plus_writers.rationale: Extreme contention. Should not occur if partitioning is applied correctly. This is a safety net.
17_plus_writers.warning: If you need this configuration, your partitioning strategy has failed. Revisit step 2.

procedures.output: Retry configuration applied to all database connections

procedures.title: Implement Work Stealing Safeguards
procedures.action: When using work stealing queues, apply single-consumer optimization to avoid thundering herd amplification.
rules: Prefer single-consumer steal pattern: one agent checks the queue, claims an item, then the next agent checks. Sequential claiming avoids 120x tail latency amplification.
If multi-consumer is required (for speed), accept p95 of ~80ms per steal operation.
Work stealing is confirmed double-steal safe (empirically validated with 10 threads, 50 items). Correctness is guaranteed; latency is the concern.
For pipeline work items, use the pipeline module rather than raw work stealing to maintain stage ordering.
procedures.output: Work stealing pattern documented (single-consumer or multi-consumer with latency acceptance)

procedures.title: Monitor Contention During Operation
procedures.action: Track SQLite operation latency during the operation. Escalate if thresholds are breached.

monitoring_thresholds.yellow: p99 35-55ms. Contention increasing. Check if writer count has exceeded plan.
monitoring_thresholds.orange: p99 55-130ms. Significant contention. Consider partitioning or reducing writers.
monitoring_thresholds.red: p99 > 130ms. Severe contention. Immediate action required: partition database, reduce concurrent writers, or switch to single-writer proxy.

procedures.monitoring_method: Coordinator checks operation latency every 30 seconds via dashboard. Log p99 values per database.
procedures.output: Contention health logged per monitoring interval

procedures.title: Handle Zombie Work Items
procedures.action: Implement timeout-based reclaim for in-progress work items to prevent deadlocks from crashed agents.

configuration.reclaim_action: Mark stale in_progress items as 'available' with a note indicating reclaim reason
configuration.notification: Log reclaimed items and notify coordinator via hub status update

procedures.rationale: No existing timeout-based reclaim exists (identified as weak link #3, severity: high). A crashed agent permanently blocks its assigned work without this safeguard.

anti_patterns.name: The Shared Database
anti_patterns.description: All agents in a 10+ agent team writing to a single SQLite database.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: At 10 concurrent writers, throughput is 5.6% of single-thread. p99 latency exceeds 130ms. The coordination system becomes the bottleneck instead of the work.
anti_patterns.fix: Partition into databases of max 4 writers each. Use sub-coordinator or single-writer proxy pattern.

anti_patterns.name: Retry Without Jitter
anti_patterns.description: Using fixed-delay retries without randomization under contention.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: Synchronized retries create periodic contention spikes. All agents retry at the same time, amplifying the thundering herd effect.
anti_patterns.fix: Always use exponential backoff WITH jitter. Add random delay of 0-50% of the backoff interval.

anti_patterns.name: Ignoring Tail Latency
anti_patterns.description: Monitoring only p50 or mean latency, which stays constant at ~0.24ms regardless of contention.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: p50 is misleading. It stays flat at all thread counts. The real problem shows in p99: 0ms at 1 thread to 230ms at 32 threads.
anti_patterns.fix: Always monitor p99 latency. Use p99 thresholds for escalation, not p50 or mean.

anti_patterns.name: Unprotected Pipeline Work Items
anti_patterns.description: Running pipelines without zombie work item reclaim.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: A crashed agent permanently blocks its work item. Downstream pipeline stages wait forever. Silent deadlock.
anti_patterns.fix: Enable timeout-based reclaim (default 30 minutes). Check for stale items every 60 seconds.

references.data_points: 6 contention levels, throughput and latency measurements
Thundering herd validation, 10 threads x 50 items
Independent contention benchmark confirming cliff at 4 threads
SQLite contention identified as primary scaling bottleneck
Zombie work items ranked #3 severity high

compliance_indicators: No database has more than 4 concurrent writers without documented partitioning plan
Retry configuration matches writer count tier
Zombie work item reclaim is enabled for all pipeline operations
p99 latency monitored and logged per database every 30 seconds
Work stealing uses single-consumer pattern unless multi-consumer latency is accepted
metrics.measurement_method: Log p99 latency and ops/sec per database per 30-second monitoring interval. Compare against contention curve. Flag any database operating above its writer-count tier threshold.
